data.narrative:
Twenty, a Series A-stage defense and security company that has raised $38M to date, sits within a sector comp universe of 10 peers (2 public, 8 private), including same-stage comparables Stark Defence, Singularity, and NODA AI.

Two valuation methods apply to this analysis. Stage-progression methodology, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies $76M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage companies yields a median valuation of $400M, though the peer set exhibits substantial dispersion: NODA AI at $125M, Singularity at $400M, and Stark Defence at $4.0B. This wide range ($125M to $4.0B) reflects meaningful heterogeneity within the defense tech space at this stage.

Triangulation of both methods supports a valuation range of $65M (low) to $460M (high), with a median point of $238M. The substantial gap between stage-progression ($76M) and peer-median ($400M) reflects uncertainty around Twenty's competitive positioning, unit economics maturity, and technology differentiation relative to the peer set. Key uncertainties include revenue traction (not provided), customer concentration, and whether Twenty's technical capabilities and market opportunity align more closely with the lower-valuation tier (NODA AI, $125M) or mid-tier peers. Additional disclosure on near-term revenue or customer commitments would materially narrow this range.
